prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json (func_metadata.py) eagerly attempts json.loads() on any string argument whose annotation isn't exactly `str`. For unions like `str | None`, this corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a plain string payload such as '{"a":1}') by silently turning them into dicts/lists, since no other member of `str | None` could ever legitimately result from decoding a string as JSON. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add a pre-check before pre_parse_json's json.loads() call, but they differ in correctness on two concrete points. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() to strip Annotated wrappers before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` (the idiomatic form for described optional params) is still recognized as skip-worthy; #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping Annotated, so any Annotated-wrapped union member still triggers pre-parsing and the corruption bug persists for that common case. prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams` (keyed by request id), cross-wiring responses between the two requests or causing one to hang. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request with an id already present in `_request_streams`, returning a 400/Bad Request instead of allowing the overwrite. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams` (keyed by request id), cross-wiring responses between the two requests or causing one to hang. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request with an id already present in `_request_streams`, returning a 400/Bad Request instead of allowing the overwrite. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3221 covers two edge cases that #3063's plain `str(message.id)` key misses: (1) JSON-RPC treats int `1` and string `"1"` as distinct ids, but `str(id)` collapses them, so #3063 would falsely 409 a string id because an int id is in flight (or vice versa) — #3221's `_request_stream_key` prefixes with `i:`/`s:` to keep them distinct; (2) a string request id equal to `"_GET_stream"` would collide with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel under #3063's scheme, letting a request lock out or share the standalone GET stream slot — #3221's keying scheme makes that collision impossible by construction. #3063's diff is smaller and simpler but doesn't handle either case.

prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held for the full duration of the yielded request in async_auth_flow, so a long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request through the same provider instance until it completes. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock is held for the full duration of the yielded request in async_auth_flow, so a long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request through the same provider instance until it completes. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3243 replaces context.lock (anyio.Lock) with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), which its own comments explain is needed because httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — on the trio backend anyio.Lock enforces same-task release and would raise in that case, while a Semaphore has no such ownership check. #2858 and #3252 both keep `lock: anyio.Lock` and only narrow where it's acquired/released around the yield point, reducing contention but retaining that same-task release requirement.

prs.author: draesthetic
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage in _initialize() never get token_expiry_time computed, so is_token_valid() treats stale/expired tokens as valid and the client is forced into a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh after every process restart. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens loaded from storage in _initialize() never get token_expiry_time computed, so is_token_valid() treats stale/expired tokens as valid and the client is forced into a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh after every process restart. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3251 makes the same _initialize() change as #1784 (calling context.update_token_expiry() on the stored token's expires_in, mirroring what set_tokens already does), and additionally restores oauth_metadata from storage via a getattr guard so _refresh_token's endpoint lookup also works after restart — it's a strict superset of #1784's diff. #2875 doesn't touch _initialize() or is_token_valid() at all; it only adds a fallback refresh attempt inside the 401 handler, so a restarted client still sends one request with a stale token and eats a round trip before that fallback runs, whereas fixing token_expiry_time lets the existing proactive-refresh branch fire before the request is even sent.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a pre-check before pre_parse_json's json.loads() call, but they differ in correctness on two concrete points. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() to strip Annotated wrappers before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` (the idiomatic form for described optional params) is still recognized as skip-worthy; #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping Annotated, so any Annotated-wrapped union member still triggers pre-parsing and the corruption bug persists for that common case. Second, #3056 scopes the skip specifically to `str | None` per its own documented reasoning ('no member of this union other than str could ever be produced by decoding a string as JSON'), whereas #2032's frozenset-based check also silently disables pre-parsing for unrelated unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, changing behavior beyond the reported corruption case.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 replaces context.lock (anyio.Lock) with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1), which its own comments explain is needed because httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock — on the trio backend anyio.Lock enforces same-task release and would raise in that case, while a Semaphore has no such ownership check. #2858 and #3252 both keep `lock: anyio.Lock` and only narrow where it's acquired/released around the yield point, reducing contention but retaining that same-task release requirement.

clusters.pick_reason: #3221 covers two edge cases that #3063's plain `str(message.id)` key misses: (1) JSON-RPC treats int `1` and string `"1"` as distinct ids, but `str(id)` collapses them, so #3063 would falsely 409 a string id because an int id is in flight (or vice versa) — #3221's `_request_stream_key` prefixes with `i:`/`s:` to keep them distinct; (2) a string request id equal to `"_GET_stream"` would collide with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel under #3063's scheme, letting a request lock out or share the standalone GET stream slot — #3221's keying scheme makes that collision impossible by construction. #3063's diff is smaller and simpler but doesn't handle either case.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams` (keyed by request id), cross-wiring responses between the two requests or causing one to hang. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request with an id already present in `_request_streams`, returning a 400/Bad Request instead of allowing the overwrite.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add a pre-check before pre_parse_json's json.loads() call, but they differ in correctness on two concrete points. #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() to strip Annotated wrappers before checking union members, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` (the idiomatic form for described optional params) is still recognized as skip-worthy; #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` without unwrapping Annotated, so any Annotated-wrapped union member still triggers pre-parsing and the corruption bug persists for that common case. Second, #3056 scopes the skip specifically to `str | None` per its own documented reasoning ('no member of this union other than str could ever be produced by decoding a string as JSON'), whereas #2032's frozenset-based check also silently disables pre-parsing for unrelated unions like `str | int` or `str | bool`, changing behavior beyond the reported corruption case.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3243: context.lock is held for the full duration of the yielded request in async_auth_flow, so a long-running request (e.g. a standalone GET SSE stream) blocks every other concurrent request through the same provider instance until it completes.

clusters.pick_reason: #3221 covers two edge cases that #3063's plain `str(message.id)` key misses: (1) JSON-RPC treats int `1` and string `"1"` as distinct ids, but `str(id)` collapses them, so #3063 would falsely 409 a string id because an int id is in flight (or vice versa) — #3221's `_request_stream_key` prefixes with `i:`/`s:` to keep them distinct; (2) a string request id equal to `"_GET_stream"` would collide with the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel under #3063's scheme, letting a request lock out or share the standalone GET stream slot — #3221's keying scheme makes that collision impossible by construction. #3063's diff is smaller and simpler but doesn't handle either case.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id silently overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams` (keyed by request id), cross-wiring responses between the two requests or causing one to hang. Both PRs add a check to reject a second in-flight request with an id already present in `_request_streams`, returning a 400/Bad Request instead of allowing the overwrite.
